kin.form: 邇邇芸命 (Ninigi-no-mikoto), 'The August Rice Spirit'

pronunciation.note: Ninigi is Tier 2: plain Hepburn. He is the heavenly grandson sent to rule the terrestrial world.

domains.title: The August Rice Spirit
domains.subtitle: Heavenly Grandson and Bearer of the Regalia
domains.lead: Ninigi is the grandson of Amaterasu, sent from heaven to rule the terrestrial world and establish the imperial line. He descended to Takachiho in Kyūshū bearing the Three Sacred Regalia — the mirror, the sword, and the jewel — and his great-grandson became Emperor Jimmu, the legendary first emperor of Japan.

cards.name: Bearer of the Regalia
cards.desc: He carried the mirror, sword, and jewel from heaven to earth.

cards.name: Heavenly Descent
cards.desc: Amaterasu sent him to rule the land of reed plains.

cards.name: Imperial Ancestor
cards.desc: His line produced Jimmu and the imperial house.

cards.name: Rice Spirit
cards.desc: His name associates him with rice and agricultural sovereignty.

mythology.lead: Ninigi's mythology is the bridge between the heavenly realm of Amaterasu and the earthly rule of the emperors.

myths.title: The Descent from Heaven
myths.text: Amaterasu decided that her grandson Ninigi should rule the terrestrial world. She gave him the Three Sacred Regalia and sent him down to Takachiho in Kyūshū. The earthly kami Ōkuninushi initially resisted but eventually submitted after negotiations and divine pressure. Ninigi thus established heavenly rule over the land.

myths.title: Marriage to Konohana-Sakuya-hime
myths.text: Ninigi met the princess Konohana-Sakuya-hime, daughter of the mountain god Ōyamatsumi, beside a blossoming tree. She promised to bear his children, but when her pregnancy was doubted, she entered a birthing hut and set it on fire, vowing that the children would survive if they were truly his. Hoderi and Hoori were born from the flames, proving her words.

myths.title: Ancestor of Jimmu
myths.text: Through his son Hoori and grandson Ugayafukiaezu, Ninigi became the great-grandfather of Kamuyamato-Iwarebiko, later known as Emperor Jimmu. The imperial line thus traces its ancestry directly to the sun goddess through Ninigi.

lore.syncretism: Ninigi is primarily an imperial genealogical figure rather than a widely worshipped deity. His role connects solar mythology, agricultural sovereignty, and political legitimacy. In State Shinto, his descent was taught as the founding event of the Japanese nation.
lore.culturalLegacy: Ninigi is remembered chiefly in imperial rites and in the mythology taught in Japanese schools. Takachiho remains a pilgrimage site associated with his descent, and the Three Sacred Regalia continue to symbolize imperial legitimacy.
lore.extendedMeditation: Ninigi is the moment when heaven touches earth. He carries divine authority not as force but as gift — the regalia, the rice, the lineage. His story asks what it means to receive power and pass it on.
lore.archaeology: Ninigi has no independent material cult. His significance is preserved in the textual genealogy of the imperial house and in sites such as Takachiho, where his descent is commemorated.
